scope: Proposition 5.2 (Averaged collision bound) of the manuscript “Ground-state condensation in the dilute hard-sphere gas” (preprints/Ground-state-condensation-in-the-dilute-hard-sphere-gas-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 267 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3f861f3b57ec1d6a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix m ≥ ℓD/2 pairs (yi, zi) with yi ∈ Bv and |zi − v| ≤ 3. Assume that each of the two endpoint lists is s0-separated. Let c be a deterministic regular torus path whose outer endpoints are at distance greater than s0 from the corresponding endpoints of every label under consideration. Then, for every target cell B, 1 m m ∑︂ i=1 QB yi,zi (Cv ∩ H(c)) ≤ Ctr + C rD3γ D √ h0 . (5.4) The same conclusion holds if c is the original path of one of these labels: omit that label’s summand and retain the divisor m, assuming endpoint separation for all the remaining labels. The constant C may depend on b, ℓ, Creg, but is independent of small t.
